Tuesday 03 November 2026 · 23 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 1.68% to 23,441 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +4.92% weighted by turnover, against +1.32% for the median stock, a gap of 3.6 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Mold-Tek Packaging Limited rose 7.2% on 102 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Borosil Limited rose 9.1% on 58 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Go Fashion (India) Limited rose 0.2% on 84 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

The exchange has formally asked 1 company to explain today's move: ITI Limited. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

What happened
Breaking
EXCLUSIVE: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute under UK trade pact, sources say
India proposed cutting import duties on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75% initially, tapering to 50% under the UK trade pact. Lower tariffs reduce landed costs, threatening gross margins for domestic liquor makers like United Spirits and Radico Khaitan through cheaper premium imports. Official publication of the finalized trade agreement terms in coming weeks will confirm the timeline and tariff glide path.
Reuters Business · +1 other
US manufacturing strengthens in October, input prices stay high
US manufacturing activity expanded in October while input price inflation accelerated, signaling persistent cost pressures in the industrial supply chain. Strong US economic data and sticky inflation reduce expectations of aggressive Federal Reserve rate cuts. This strengthens the US dollar, exerting downward pressure on the rupee and increasing risk of foreign portfolio outflows from Indian financial and IT equities.
Reuters Business · +2 others
A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
Bank of India raised term deposit rates by up to 50 basis points, following systemic liquidity shifting into deficit. Shrinkage in banking liquidity forces lenders to bid up deposit rates to sustain credit growth. Higher cost of deposits will compress net interest margins across public and private sector banks over the next two quarters, unless asset yields reprice upward proportionately.
ET Markets · +2 others
Connected to your data
Mold-Tek Packaging shares surge 17% as Q2 FY 27 profit jumps 35% YoY to Rs 21 crore
Mold-Tek Packaging reported Q2 net profit of 21 crore rupees, up 35.5% year-on-year, driven by 30.5% revenue growth. Volume expansion in food and pharmaceutical packaging improved capacity utilization and gross margins for the rigid packaging maker. Continued raw material cost pass-through will determine whether operating margins hold at these expanded levels in subsequent quarters.
ET Markets
Your themes
Meta eyes at least $20 billion from potential bond offerings, Bloomberg News reports
Meta plans to raise 20 billion dollars through cross-border bond offerings to fund artificial intelligence capital expenditure, a transaction that has no direct transmission mechanism to Indian equities.
AI & data centresET Markets · +1 other
200% revenue growth, 14X profit: 2 niche stocks riding the global data centre boom - The Financial Express
Surging demand for domestic data center infrastructure drove a two-fold revenue increase and fourteen-fold net profit expansion for niche equipment suppliers during the recent quarter. Rapid data center buildouts boost order inflow and operating leverage for listed electrical equipment, transformer, and cooling providers like Schneider Electric Infrastructure. Quarterly capital expenditure announcements from major cloud providers will confirm the multi-year sustainability of this order cycle.
AI & data centresData centres and AI capex · +1 other
Avaada Electro secures ALMM enlistment for 7.1 GW solar cell capacity - Renewable Watch
Avaada Electro secured government enlistment under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers for 7.1 GW of solar cell manufacturing capacity. Enlistment enables domestic solar project developers to source these cells for government-subsidized tenders. This increases local cell availability for module makers like Premier Energies, easing input sourcing constraints and supporting gross margins across domestic solar EPC contracts.
Green energy & solarSolar and green energy
Anthropic revenue jumps 1,100% ahead of IPO as AI spending commitments near $900 billion
Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $17 billion alongside a $23.3 billion net loss and $895 billion in future spending commitments. Massive AI infrastructure burn highlights widening cash deficits among foundational model builders. For Indian IT services majors, sustained hyperscaler capex supports enterprise cloud migration deal pipelines, though monetization delays risk deferring client discretionary tech spending in coming quarters.
AI & data centresET Markets
Saatvik Green Energy starts 1.3 GW solar module production in Odisha - scanx.trade
Saatvik Green Energy commissioned a 1.3 GW solar module production plant in Odisha. Expanding domestic module capacity aids project execution for utility-scale developers like NTPC Green Energy and Tata Power. However, rising unlisted manufacturing capacity increases supply competition, placing price pressure on realizations for listed solar module makers in subsequent quarters.
Green energy & solarSolar and green energy
Capital markets
CM dedicates Rs 432cr treatment plants for clean water in 316 Patiala villages - The Times of India
This local public water project is financially immaterial to listed Indian equities.
Water infrastructure
India markets regulator issues rules for depositary receipts on REITs, InvITs units
The Securities and Exchange Board of India issued a framework allowing REITs and InvITs to issue depositary receipts abroad. This decision enables listed entities such as Embassy Office Parks REIT and PowerGrid InvIT to tap global capital markets directly. Broader foreign investor participation could reduce borrowing costs and improve equity valuations across listed yield-bearing infrastructure vehicles.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Surge in Reliance lifts Sensex by 1.6%; Nifty tops 23,400
Reliance Industries led a 1.6 percent rally in the Sensex to take the Nifty past 23,400, supported by net foreign institutional inflows and lower Brent crude prices. Declining crude eases raw material costs for paint, chemical, and tyre manufacturers while improving fuel marketing margins for oil refiners. Sustained daily FII net buying data over the next week will confirm whether foreign liquidity is turning structurally positive.

Macro and economy
S&P 500, Nasdaq reverse gains to close down; Apple reports
US equities closed lower after intraday gains dissolved, led by cautious trading in mega-cap technology stocks ahead of Apple's earnings report. Weakness in US tech valuations typically spills over to Indian IT exporters through reduced discretionary IT spending and subdued ADR sentiment for Infosys and Wipro. First-quarter revenue guidance from major US enterprise software clients will indicate whether Indian IT deal pipelines face further delays.
Reuters Business
Sebi cuts cool-off period for OFS by off-market illiquid Invits to 8 weeks
Sebi shortened the required cooling-off period for offer-for-sale transactions in privately listed, illiquid Infrastructure Investment Trusts to eight weeks from twelve weeks. The regulatory change improves primary market liquidity and capital recycling velocity for infrastructure sponsors and private equity funds holding unlisted asset vehicles. Upcoming institutional secondary placement volumes in private InvITs will show if sponsors actively utilize the shorter lock-in window.
BS Markets · +1 other
Capex key to India's growth strategy, fiscal prudence remains top priority: Sitharaman at HSBC event
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman reaffirmed that public capital expenditure will drive economic growth while the government maintains its stated fiscal deficit reduction trajectory. Continued budgetary support for infrastructure directly sustains order book execution for capital goods, cement, and engineering companies like Larsen & Toubro. Monthly central government expenditure statements will confirm whether actual capital outlay matches the budget allocations in the second half.
ET Economy
S&P 500 ends down; Apple dips ahead of quarterly report
Wall Street benchmarks closed lower as Apple slipped prior to its quarterly report, weighing on broader US equity sentiment. The resulting risk-off stance in global markets tempers near-term foreign portfolio allocation toward emerging market equities, including India. Overnight movement in the US dollar index and US Treasury yields will signal whether foreign capital flows into Indian equities remain constrained.
Reuters Business
Companies and earnings
Stocks in news: ITC, Marico, SBI, Yatra Online, NSE, Container Corp and Sun Pharma
Mixed second-quarter results saw ITC report lower consolidated net profit due to pressure in its core cigarette segment, while Marico posted strong earnings growth driven by domestic volume recovery. FMCG earnings highlight diverging margin trajectories, as raw material cost pressures affect tobacco and agricultural inputs while lower edible oil costs aid packaged goods firms. Volume growth numbers in upcoming rural consumer demand updates will determine sector valuation trajectory.
ET Markets
Marico Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 31% YoY to Rs 550 crore, revenue rises 12%
Marico expanded its Q2 operating margin to 18.2%, pushing EBITDA up 27% to Rs 709 crore alongside 12% revenue growth. Price hikes in core coconut oil combined with stabilizing copra input costs expanded gross margins, signaling earnings resilience across domestic FMCG peers like Dabur and Godrej Consumer. Rural volume growth data in coming quarters will confirm whether this recovery is volume-led.
ET Markets
FPIs are buying again. Why is their share of Indian stocks still falling?
Foreign portfolio investors reduced their holdings in 57% of top 100 large-cap companies during the September quarter, despite net aggregate inflows. Domestic mutual fund inflows expanded total market capitalization faster than foreign buying, diluting foreign ownership shares. This structural shift insulates large-cap valuations from capital flight, though financial and IT stocks remain exposed to foreign flows.
Mint Markets
US stocks today: Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as AI worries persist
The Nasdaq fell over 1% as Oracle planned $20 billion in debt to fund artificial intelligence capital expenditures. Softer US technology sentiment directly threatens client spending budgets for Indian IT exporters like TCS and Infosys. Lower crude oil prices mitigate this risk by reducing input costs for domestic paint and tile manufacturers.
ET Markets
Geopolitics
China’s 5,000-ton digging machines are a trade war risk to India
China restricted exports of heavy tunnel-boring machines and specialized construction equipment. Indian infrastructure developers like Larsen & Toubro face potential project delays and elevated capital expenditure if forced to source costlier European machinery for Himalayan road and tunnel projects. Import clearance timelines at Indian ports will confirm the operational severity of these restrictions.
ET Economy · +1 other
China Boosts Use of Stock Support Tools to Stabilize Market
China expanded liquidity facilities and eased loan terms for financial institutions using stock-buying tools. State-backed equity intervention in Beijing risks diverting tactical foreign fund flows away from India, given India's premium valuation relative to emerging market peers. China's net foreign portfolio flow data in coming weeks will confirm if capital reallocation occurs.
Mint Markets
US midterm elections: How a Democratic victory could impact defence, healthcare, crypto and AI stocks
Speculative policy outcomes from US midterm elections carry no direct operational impact on Indian equities or foreign capital flows.
